## New Investigation Ideas

- **[2026-10-24] Fred's whole automation stack is 30 scheduled-task prompts, and none of them is under version control. Today's newly listened podcast says that is the first thing to fix, because a model upgrade can quietly make a skill worse.** [[podcasts/podcast-growth-podcast-effective-loops-in-claude]] (Tyler Folkman on *The Growth Podcast*) gives two rules for Claude Code loops: make the validation gate deterministic, and keep skills in version control so you can roll back when a model change degrades them. `C:\Users\Mike\.claude\scheduled-tasks\` holds 30 task folders and has no `.git`. Two things the wiki already records make this more than theory. First, memory/index.md Key Decisions says `update_scheduled_task` *overwrites* SKILL.md, and that portfolio-management-briefing keeps its full instructions in SKILL.md with a "never call update" rule as the only protection. Second, the 2026-10-10 root cause of the fabricated trade was wording inside a briefing task's instructions (autonomous Turso-write steps), found only by reconstruction because there was no diff history to look at. The market-watchlist pipeline and fred-dashboard are already in private GitHub repos, so the habit exists; it just stops at the prompts. This differs from the 2026-10-13 pre-flight-check idea, which is about the *gate* on data; this is about the *instructions* themselves. **Next step:** `git init` the scheduled-tasks folder (private remote, or local only), commit the current state as a baseline, and add a one-line note to memory/index.md Key Decisions. Then, when a task's output changes character, `git log -p` on its SKILL.md/instructions.md shows whether the prompt changed or the model did. Check first that no task folder holds secrets (.env, tokens) before pushing anywhere.

## New Cross-Domain Connections

- **[2026-10-24] The guest Fred just listened to has spent ten years arguing that the half of the Magic Formula Fred's Strategy A relies on, the ROIC "quality" leg, is the half that loses money. Strategy A is now 1 for 12.** [[podcasts/podcast-behind-the-balance-sheet-tobias-carlisle]] is Tobias Carlisle's case that value is due a comeback. His acquirer's multiple (EV ÷ operating earnings) is Greenblatt's earnings yield turned upside down, with the return-on-capital ranking removed. In his published work (*Deep Value*, 2014) he reports that ranking on cheapness alone beat the full Magic Formula in backtests. His reason is mean reversion: a very high ROIC usually means peak margins, so the formula's "good *and* cheap" intersection keeps picking cyclicals at their earnings peak. [[books/book-little-book-beats-market]] presents that same intersection as the formula's whole edge. Fred's own results match Carlisle's warning more than Greenblatt's promise. [[finance/models/model-portfolio-management]] shows Strategy A at 1/12. Its 10-04 review found half the new Magic Formula passes were precious-metals miners, and the 10-11 review proposed a Materials-sector guard on the candidate query. The 10-19 idea above flagged CF Industries (P/E 8.6, ROIC 24.5%) as a likely peak-earnings cyclical. The sector guard is a patch on the symptom, while Carlisle names the cause, and the two give a testable choice. Re-rank the last ~12 Strategy A entries by EV/EBIT alone and see whether the cyclicals drop out or rise. If they rise, the guard is the right fix. If they fall away, ROIC is the leg doing the damage. The capital-cap exits still confound realised returns, so use the 10-04 forward-return method, not closed P&L.

## Podcast Books

2 new: *Soldier of Fortune* (Tobias Carlisle), *The Art of War* (Sun Tzu), both from Behind the Balance Sheet #64.

## New Investigation Ideas

- **[2026-10-23] The live portfolio still labels Flutter a "🟢 Burry-aligned long", but Burry sold all of it on 09-11.** [[finance/trading-portfolio]]'s Burry-signal table gives FLUT the reason "Burry long at $100.72 (Jul 24 2026); anti-prediction-markets thesis", and the 10-22 briefing kept the last share on Watch with that label. [[finance/investor-letters/source-burry-trading-post-2026-09-11]] says he sold the whole position. His reason was price: it was no longer cheap next to names that had fallen further, and he moved most of the money into LULU under $100. The briefing has not noticed. **Next step:** re-label FLUT in the signal table to "Burry exited 09-11 (valuation, thesis not withdrawn)". Then decide whether the free-ride share still has a reason to be held. Also check [[finance/michael-burry/cross-reference]] for other rows that went stale when he sold. (Only ~€0.89 is at stake. The concern is that briefing labels get copied forward without being checked.)

## New Cross-Domain Connections

- **[2026-10-23] Fred's game already measures "home advantage", and Sports Betting's unread research paper measures the same thing in real leagues.** [[games/terrain-autobattler-map-pipeline]] rejects a map if any faction's win rate is more than 5 points off its pool average over 2,000 fights (D-035). Each faction has a home terrain, so the match map shifts which side is favoured ([[games/terrain-autobattler-factions-units-economy]]). That is a home-advantage test with a significance threshold. [[sports-betting/markets]] lists "public bias toward home teams" as its first edge source but has no way to measure it. The uningested paper `raw/sports-betting/Scoring dynamics across professional team sports tempo, balance and predictability - EPJ Data Science.md` uses the same quantity: "balance" is the share of scoring events each team wins, modelled as a biased Bernoulli process. It finds real NFL/college football games vary more than a fair coin would explain. The harness Fred built for map balance (fixed seeds, per-condition win rate against a baseline, a 5-point rejection gate) is the template for a first Sports Betting model page. It would estimate home bias per league, then check whether bookmaker 1X2 prices over- or under-price it.
